claim: GIAS distinguishes mandatory Requirements, nonmandatory implementation considerations and nonexclusive evidence examples.
The audit plan is based on documented at-least-annual organisational risk assessment, remains dynamic, and its significant changes require board approval.
Coordination and consideration of reliance are required; actual reliance is conditional and documented.
CAE establishes and updates methodologies; their form can vary and no particular software is mandated.
Engagement work can overlap and iterate; appropriate supervision/responsibilities may be delegated with CAE accountability retained.
Specific advisory exceptions qualify formal risk assessment, criteria and evidence-for-findings obligations, without blanket exemption.
Engagement objectives, scope, criteria and resources have documented, contextual requirements and change/approval duties.
A documented work programme identifies criteria, tasks, methods/tools and assigned auditors, with prior and prompt change approval under 13.6.
Information must be relevant, reliable and sufficient; inadequacy can require further collection or affect findings/conclusions.
Potential findings require evaluation; root-cause identification is qualified by feasibility, with recommendation/action-plan alternatives.
Conclusions address objectives and aggregate significance; assurance adds effectiveness considerations.
Engagement documentation supports informed repetition and results, review and retention; software/template choices vary.
Final communication has content, quality, approval and appropriate-recipient requirements, with assurance-specific additions.
Follow-up confirms implementation risk-basedly; management risk acceptance and CAE escalation are distinct from remediation.
Skepticism and information-use/confidentiality duties apply; they do not by themselves prescribe a security architecture.
The 12-month presumption concerns prior responsibility; prior advisory service has separate objectivity assessment provisions.
DomainIII Essential Conditions require actor-specific treatment including CAE discussion and documented alternatives, not blanket optionality.
SR 26-2 and OCC 2026-13 were issued 2026-04-17 and updated earlier model-risk supervisory guidance.
Joint model-risk guidance excludes generative/agentic AI and is nonprescriptive, but does not exempt tools from all applicable governance/law.
GIAS was issued 2024-01-09 and effective 2025-01-09.
Three-cycle/six-stage and three/four-layer maps are useful analytical arrangements, not demonstrated universal practitioner taxonomies.
GIAS imposes a universal 5–20% sample norm or fixed 25/40 sample size.
GIAS mandates a universal RCM or five-Cs template.
GIAS requires the CAE personally to click every digital approval gate.
Every finding must have a known root cause without feasibility qualification.
